This course is designed for learners who want to develop a solid understanding of statistical concepts and methods for interpreting research studies, without requiring programming skills. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of mathematical concepts and a familiarity with research design. The course covers topics such as descriptive and inferential statistics, hypothesis testing, and regression analysis, with a focus on applying statistical concepts to real-world research scenarios. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and case studies, learners will gain the skills to critically evaluate research findings, identify biases, and make informed decisions based on data-driven evidence. The target duration of this course is approximately 12 weeks, with a total of 48 hours of instruction.

expanded_query: To develop a strong foundation in financial accounting and effectively interpret a company's annual report, this course covers the fundamental principles and concepts of financial accounting, including financial statement preparation, asset valuation, and liability recognition. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of business operations and accounting principles, typically acquired through introductory accounting courses. The course will focus on the skills and topics necessary to analyze and interpret financial statements, including the ability to identify and record financial transactions, prepare and present financial reports, and apply Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) to ensure accurate and transparent financial reporting. Upon completion, learners will be able to read and understand a company's annual report, including the balance sheet, income statement, and cash flow statement.

expanded_query: This course provides foundational knowledge in human anatomy and physiology, specifically designed to prepare students for a nursing program. Prerequisites include a basic understanding of biology and chemistry. Through a combination of lectures, discussions, and hands-on activities, students will develop skills in identifying and describing the structure and function of the human body, including the skeletal, muscular, and nervous systems, as well as the circulatory, respiratory, and digestive systems. The course will also cover the principles of homeostasis, cellular respiration, and the nervous and endocrine systems, with a focus on clinical applications relevant to nursing practice.
